findings.where: First screen, the contact row under the paragraphs: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action is dead. 'Write to me' is drawn as a filled button and the address is underlined like a link, but neither does anything when clicked or tapped. The parts map lists both as static, and the hover rule changes them as though they act. The only working contact is the small address link in the footer, at the very end of the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark. They click the most prominent button on the screen, or tap the address on a phone, and nothing happens. Getting in touch is the page's job, so this stops the task.

findings.where: First screen, 'Book a consultation': a filled blue button with the same weight as 'Write to me', linking to #consult
findings.fault: There are two equal primary actions where the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark. The second one also promises a booking flow that a brochure site has no way to provide: it jumps to an anchor, and no consultation or booking section appears anywhere on the page. As the page stands, it is the only one of the two buttons that does anything, and it does nothing useful.
findings.who_objects: The visitor has to choose between two identical buttons and gets no booking. The founder would also object, because the brief's personal-advisor test asks for one direct way to reach Mark, and a 'Book a consultation' button reads like any consultancy's sales funnel.

findings.where: First screen, the margin notes (Istanbul 2025 / Best Practices in PPP Legislation…, Melbourne 2026 / LLM Course on PPP Law…, São Paulo 2024 / New Approaches to Risk Allocation…); the same blue on the specimen section labels (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The margin notes are set in the house blue, which the palette names as the link colour, and they read as titles of real talks. That makes them look like links to those talks or their slides, but they are static. The specimen labels take the same reserved link colour, so on this page the blue means both 'link' and 'label'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to read the Istanbul or Melbourne talk clicks the title and nothing happens. The talks exist as PDFs on Mark's site, so a link is exactly what the visitor expects to find there. Angélique, publishing later pages, inherits a blue that no longer tells a reader what can be clicked.

findings.where: Header navigation: Profile, Articles and Presentations, Blog
findings.fault: The nav items are working links to #profile, #articles and #blog, but none of those sections exists on the page, so a click goes nowhere. Of particular note, 'Articles and Presentations' does not reach the PDF list that the brief calls the product.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants to check Mark's record before writing to him picks Profile or Articles and gets no response. The workaround is scrolling, but that does not find a profile section either.
